paras: The Tracy City cabin shooting was an attack on June 11, 1881, in which unknown parties fired into the cabin of a Black man at Tracy City, Tennessee. No deaths or injuries were reported, and the case drew notice because Governor Hawkins offered a reward for the attackers.

According to the Nashville American, the attackers fired into the cabin of "a colored man" at Tracy City on "the 11th inst." The item did not name the man, give the number of attackers, or say whether anyone inside was hurt. It described the shooting as having been done "without cause or provocation" and reported no accusation against the man.
Governor Hawkins offered a reward of $250 for the apprehension and conviction of each of the "unknown parties" involved. No report of arrests, an indictment or a trial appears in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single sentence in the "Pencilettes" column of the Knoxville Daily Chronicle of June 19, 1881, credited to the Nashville American. The Chronicle ran it between notes on census appointments and local produce, presenting it as a routine item of state news framed around the governor's reward. By repeating the phrase "without cause or provocation," the item placed the blame on the attackers rather than on the man whose home was shot into.
